level1.text: The distance $s$ travelled by a trolley was measured as a function of time $t$, and the line fitted to the data points passes through the points $(1.0\,\text{s};\ 2.3\,\text{m})$ and $(7.0\,\text{s};\ 10.1\,\text{m})$. What is the slope of the line? Give the answer in m/s.

Water is let into a swimming pool. According to the measurements, the height $h$ of the water as a function of time $t$ follows the line $h = 0.50\,\tfrac{\text{cm}}{\text{min}} \cdot t + 12\,\text{cm}$. How high is the water surface when the tap has been open for 30 minutes? Give the answer in centimetres.

The height $h$ of a lawn was followed as a function of days $t$, and the fitted line is $h = 0.60\,\tfrac{\text{cm}}{\text{day}} \cdot t + 4.0\,\text{cm}$. On which day from the start of the measurements is the lawn 10 cm tall? Give the answer in days.

A candle burns steadily. The line fitted to the data points passes through the points $(0.0\,\text{h};\ 20.0\,\text{cm})$ and $(4.0\,\text{h};\ 14.0\,\text{cm})$, with the length of the candle on the $y$-axis. What is the slope of the line? Give the answer with its sign in cm/h.

The mass $m$ of a stack of copy paper is directly proportional to the number of sheets $N$, so the mass is represented by a line through the origin. When $N = 250$, the mass is $1.2\,\text{kg}$. What is the mass of one sheet? Give the answer in grams.

level2.text: The distance $s$ travelled by a cyclist was measured in kilometres and the time $t$ in minutes. The line fitted to the data points passes through the points $(2.0\,\text{min};\ 0.30\,\text{km})$ and $(10.0\,\text{min};\ 1.50\,\text{km})$. What is the slope of the line in m/s?

The height $h$ of the surface in a water tank increases steadily as a function of time $t$. The fitted line passes through the points $(2.0\,\text{min};\ 7.0\,\text{cm})$ and $(6.0\,\text{min};\ 15.0\,\text{cm})$. How high is the surface at 10.0 minutes, when the line is extended beyond the measured range? Give the answer in centimetres.

The combined mass $m$ of a water canister and the water in it was measured as a function of the volume $V$ of the water. The fitted line passes through the points $(3.0\,\text{l};\ 3.9\,\text{kg})$ and $(9.0\,\text{l};\ 9.9\,\text{kg})$. What is the mass of the empty canister? Give the answer in kilograms.

The price of a taxi ride is a starting charge of $4.0\,\text{€}$ plus $2.5\,\text{€}$ for every kilometre driven. The price is a function of the distance, $y = kx + b$. How many times as expensive is a 10 km ride as a 5.0 km ride? Give the answer as a number.

level3.text: A student measured the position $s$ of a trolley as a function of time $t$, but started the stopwatch only when the trolley had already travelled some distance from the start of the track. The line fitted to the data points is $s = 0.85\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}} \cdot t + 0.40\,\text{m}$, where $s$ is measured from the start of the track. What time on the stopwatch corresponds to the moment when the trolley was at the start of the track ($s = 0$)? Give the answer in seconds with its sign and justify the sign.

The temperature $T$ of coffee was measured as a function of time $t$: $0\,\text{min}$: $90\,{}^\circ\text{C}$, $10\,\text{min}$: $72\,{}^\circ\text{C}$, $20\,\text{min}$: $60\,{}^\circ\text{C}$ and $30\,\text{min}$: $51\,{}^\circ\text{C}$. How many times greater is the change in temperature per minute (the absolute value of the slope) in the first ten-minute interval than in the last? Justify why one line does not describe all the measurements.

Two points are read from the line $y = 2.0\,x$, and the reading error of each $y$ value is at most $0.1$ units. The slope is calculated either from the points $x = 4.0$ and $x = 4.5$ or from the points $x = 1.0$ and $x = 9.0$. How many times greater is the relative uncertainty of the slope when it is calculated from the close points? Use the worst case, in which the reading errors add up in the difference $\Delta y$. Justify why points far apart are the better choice.
